transcript: These are the top three stories of all time. 3. 1984 by George Orwell. Orwell's dystopian novel portrays a totalitarian society suppressing individuality and controlling truth. Its themes of surveillance and governmental control remain eerily relevant, provoking critical discussions about freedom and manipulation. 2. The Odyssey by Homer. This ancient Greek epic follows Odysseus' arduous journey home from the Trojan War, encounter mythical creatures and God's wrath. Homer's narrative prowess and heroic themes define Western literature. 1. Watch till the very end for a bonus. Romeo and Juliet by William Shakespeare. This tragic tale of star-crossed lovers Romeo and Juliet set in feuding Verona families remains a timeless classic. Shakespeare's exploration of love, conflict, and fate resonates globally.
